newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends near session lows.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends near session lows.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures ended Friday near session lows in razor-thin trade following an uninspired New York performance.
Prices were locked in a tight $11-$14 band and switches were also little changed. "August is normally a quiet month," said one.
Even forecasts calling for a cold front in Brazil's coffee belt late next week failed to impress the London market.
Benchmark September, which spent the afternoon $19 lower at $1,620, dipped to $1,618 at the close for a $23 loss.
November fell to a low of $1,609 before ending the day $21 down at $1,610.
Volume reached 2,611 lots. Sept/Nov switches were traded at around $10, little-changed from the previous sessions.
Traders said the London market was likely to continue its hold just over the $1,600 level on September.
"But it depends on what New York does. It does look a bit weak now.
Talk about the cold weather in Brazil has dissipated for now, suggesting that coffee could come under further selling pressure.
But traders said sellers were probably quite hesitant today in case the weather outlook changed over the weekend.

Towards the close on Friday, weather forecaster Cropcast said long-range guidance models showed the greatest threat of cold weather reaching Brazil's coffee belt will be toward the middle of next week, with the probability of a freeze set at 20 percent.

"The latest long-range model forecast guidance is now suggesting that the threat of freezing temperatures will be greatest during the middle of next week instead of the weekend," Cropcast said in its daily weather summary.

However, forecaster Weather Services Corp said in its daily update that while somewhat cooler temperatures could reach Brazil's coffee belt during the second half of the week, a high pressure expected to build in Argentina next week is likely to pass well to the south of coffee growing areas.
